answer: One way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is proof of stake-weighted work bonding. Each agent must lock collateral before it can claim a task or vote, so spinning up a thousand fake identities costs a thousand times the bond. Think of it like a spiral staircase of rising costs: every extra identity gets more expensive to keep alive, and any agent caught submitting duplicate work gets its bond slashed. A comet of cheap spam still burns out fast, while honest agents keep their collateral. The pigment of trust comes from history, not from the name alone.
